stem: Who was the founder of Chola dynasty?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/ More than one of the above

expl: The Chola empire was founded by Vijayalaya, who initially was a feudatory chief of the Pallavas. Around 850 CE, he captured Tanjore. The Shaiva temple at Tanjore— Rajarajeshwara (or Brihadishwara) Temple—was built during the reign of Rajaraja I.

stem: The Chola age was most famous for:

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The most notable feature of Chola rule is seen in the functioning of autonomous village institutions. In fact, during this period, villages were complete units of local self-government, and village administration was carried out by the villagers themselves.

stem: Which dynasty built the Kailasanatha Temple and in which state?
expl: The Kailasanatha (Kailasanathar) Temple is located in Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu. It was built under the patronage of the Pallava rulers.

stem: Which of the following temples is located in Kanchipuram?
expl: Ekambareswarar Temple is located in Kanchipuram. It is dedicated to Mahadeva (Shiva). The temple was built during the period of the Pallava rulers. It is noteworthy that this temple is thousands of years old. Various inscriptions from the Pallava period to the period of the Nayaka rulers have been found here. On the basis of available archaeological evidence, it can be said that the major construction work of this temple was carried out during the times of the Pallavas, the Cholas, and the Vijayanagara rulers.

stem: The Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur was constructed by which king?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The Brihadeeswarar Temple is a Hindu temple located in the Thanjavur district of Tamil Nadu, built in the early 11th century. The temple was constructed between 1003 and 1010 CE by the Chola ruler Rajaraja I. It is also known as the Rajarajeshwara Temple. The temple was built in the Dravidian style of architecture.

stem: Which of the following was the capital of the Chera dynasty ?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The Chera dynasty ruled the south-western part of South India (present-day Kerala and some parts of Tamil Nadu). According to the Kerala State Gazetteer, the Cheras’ capital Vanchi is also mentioned, which some scholars identify with Karur/Kuruvur. The earliest Chera king whose name is first mentioned in sources was Udayanjeral (Uthiyan Cheral).

stem: Which of the following dynasties is not mentioned in Sangam literature?
expl: Sangam literature provides accounts of the origin and development of the Chola, Chera, and Pandya rulers. Even though fixing the exact reign periods of various kings is difficult, Sangam literature throws sufficient light on political activities from the south of the Krishna River up to the far southern peninsula. The Kadamba dynasty is not mentioned in Sangam literature.

stem: Why was ‘Uraiyur’ famous in Sangam Era?

options.label: a
options.text: An important trade centre of spices

options.label: b
options.text: An important trade centre of cotton

options.label: c
options.text: An important centre of foreign trade

options.label: d
options.text: An important centre of domestic trade

expl: Uraiyur was an important Sangam-period city situated on the banks of the Kaveri River in Tiruchirappalli (Tamil Nadu). In the Sangam age, Uraiyur was a major centre for cotton textiles. In the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea, it is mentioned by the name Argaru.

stem: The attractive doors of the temples of South India are called-

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/ More than one of the above

expl: The attractive gateway of South Indian temples is called 'Gopuram'. The Dravidian style flourished during the Pallava, Pandya, and Chola periods. In the Pandya period, temples were comparatively small, but many enclosure walls were built around their courtyards. Their entrance gateways, called gopurams, later became grand, massive structures richly decorated with sculpture. The Chola rulers built magnificent temples as well as huge gopurams.

stem: Who established trade relations with Roman Empire?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: India’s trade with the Roman Empire began during the Sangam period with the Chera state. Many Roman objects have been found from Arikamedu.

stem: During whose reign did the Persian traveller ‘Abdur Razzaq’ come to India?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The Persian envoy Abdur Razzaq came to Vijayanagar during the reign of Devaraya II (tenure: 1422–1446 CE), the most powerful ruler of the Sangama dynasty. In his travel account Matla’ al-Sa‘dayn wa Majma‘ al-Bahrayn, he described the reign of Devaraya II.
